newsitem.title: USA: Durable goods orders up 4.6 percent in September.
newsitem.headline: Durable goods orders up 4.6 percent in September.

text.p: Orders for expensive manufactured goods jumped in September, the Commerce Department said Friday, as strong demand more than erased a very weak showing in the prior month.

The department said new orders for durable goods rose 4.6 percent, the largest increase in nearly four years, to a seasonally adjusted $174.1 billion after declining a revised 3.5 percent decline in August.
The increase far outstripped Wall Street estimates of a 2.0 percent rise.
Previously, the department said that August orders had declined 3.2 percent.
Overall orders posted the largest increase since December, 1992.
Transportation equipment showed the largest increase, moving up 17.5 percent to $44.1 billion, with half the increase accounted for by aircraft and parts.
Orders for electronic and other equipment, up in three of the last four months, rose 1.9 percent, while industrial machinery and equipment decreased 0.9 percent.
Primary metals also declined, falling 1.7 percent, after dropping 4.0 percent in August.

Orders for durable goods, such as cars, planes and home appliances intended to last at least three years, are viewed by economists as a measure of the vitality of the manufacturing sector, a powerful influence on the overall economy.

The manufacturing sector has been expanding in recent months, although it is generally believed that the U.S. economy is slowing from a very strong pace earlier in the year. Moreover, orders can by highly volatile on a month-to-month basis.
The department said defence capital goods orders rose 7.9 percent, the fourth increase in the last five months, following a 2.0 percent rise in August.
Non-defence capital goods orders, an indicator of investment in new equipment by business, zoomed up 14.1 percent following a 10.4 percent retreat in August.
Shipments of durable goods, a measure of current demand in manufacturing industries, increased 1.4 percent after rising 0.4 percent in August.
